newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shrs end mixed, foreigners largely absent.
newsitem.headline: Lima shrs end mixed, foreigners largely absent.

text.p: Shares on the Lima stock exchange closed mixed Tuesday ending a four-day run of successive rises as foreign investors were noticeably absent from the market, brokers said.
The absence of foreign players - believed to be concentrating their funds on U.S. markets - led to reduced demand for blue chip stocks, which generally fell, brokers said.
With local investors dominating the market, they continued to find bargains in second- and third-tier stocks, which they bought heavily, the brokers added.
The market was expected to fall overall Wednesday as blue chips were seen slipping again without the compensation from secondary stocks shown Tuesday, they added.
Tuesday, the General Index rose 0.84 percent to 1,543.9 points, while the blue-chip Selective Index .ISEL dipped 0.61 percent to 2,070.2 points, according to preliminary stock figures.
In a total of 2,724 operations, 54 stocks rose, 34 fell and 28 were stable. Volume was a 33.8 million ($13.6 million).
